root_cause: The Debian Packages job's apt-get install step inside the Docker container lost outbound DNS resolution partway through 'apt-get update', failing to resolve archive.ubuntu.com, azure.archive.ubuntu.com, and security.ubuntu.com repeatedly over roughly 3.5 minutes before apt gave up and used stale/no index data, causing 'wget', 'lsb-release', 'gnupg' and 'ca-certificates' to be unavailable. This is a transient DNS/networking failure in the container's network namespace or the Azure-hosted mirror infrastructure, not a problem with the PR's code changes (which only touch CPU/ARM softmax kernel source and tests, unrelated to packaging).
reproduction_steps: N/A - transient CI network/DNS failure inside the Debian Packages Docker container; not reproducible deterministically. Re-running the job typically succeeds.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Debian Packages' job; this is the 4th occurrence of the same DNS resolution failure signature in the last ~2 days.
Consider adding retry/backoff logic around apt-get update in job_debian_packages.yml to tolerate transient DNS failures.
If this recurs frequently, investigate whether the self-hosted runner's Docker network configuration or DNS resolver (e.g., /etc/resolv.conf injection) is flaky for the ubuntu24 container image.
prevention_strategies: Add a retry wrapper (e.g., 3 attempts with backoff) around 'apt-get update' and 'apt-get install' in the Debian Packages job definition to absorb transient DNS blips without failing the whole merge-queue run. Consider pinning to a local/cached apt mirror to reduce dependency on external DNS during CI.
historical_context: This exact signature (DNS resolution failures for Ubuntu archive mirrors during the Debian Packages job) has now been recorded 4 times: 2026-11-11T14:34:10Z (run 43030484756), 2026-11-11T15:36:49Z (run 43040586616), 2026-11-11T16:05:55Z (run 43040586954), and this run. A related but distinct connection-timeout variant (pattern 7d2e2ff59d37c6b4) has recurred 9 times separately. This is a known, recurring transient infrastructure/network issue affecting the merge queue.
